description: The edge forwards Expect: 100-continue unchanged on the stream (MCPWARP.md §4.1). The agent never sends a 1xx: the first bytes it writes are the app's final response. The app's request carries every end-to-end header except expect and content-length (§4.6 Request → handler). MCPWARP.md §4
in:
POST /mcp HTTP/1.1
Host: notes-tester.mcpwarp.test
accept: application/json, text/event-stream
content-type: application/json
expect: 100-continue
mcp-session-id: abc
user-agent: Go-http-client/1.1
Content-Length: 46

{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":3,"method":"tools/list"}
out:
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
content-type: application/json
Transfer-Encoding: chunked

2e
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":3,"method":"tools/list"}
0
notes: A runner fails the fixture if any HTTP/1.1 1xx status line (100 Continue included) precedes the 200. Chunk boundaries are not normative; compare the de-chunked body.
